title: SAT: SEBI Cannot Refuse an Open Offer Withdrawal Through an Unreasoned Letter
case_name: Marwadi Chandarana Intermediaries Pvt. Ltd. v. Securities and Exchange Board of India
card_summary: The acquirer had agreed to buy a stake in TruCap Finance that triggered a mandatory open offer, then terminated the deal citing a material adverse effect clause over a drop in TruCap's net worth. SEBI's letter, framed as mere comments on the draft offer letter, functioned as a refusal to let the acquirer withdraw. SAT set it aside, holding a decision with civil consequences needs reasons, and remanded it.
card_tip: Treat any SEBI communication that affects an open offer as an order in substance, whatever label it carries, and insist on a reasoned decision before complying with it or challenging it.
verification_notes: Parties, the May 2025 acquisition agreement, the September 2025 termination on material adverse effect grounds, SEBI's January 2026 letter, and SAT's 8 July 2026 order remanding the matter for a reasoned decision are consistent across LiveLawBiz, Free Press Journal and the order copy uploaded by LiveLawBiz. SAT did not decide whether the material adverse effect clause itself justified withdrawal; that question was left open on remand.
